back: Producing goods or services with the least waste of materials, time, stock, space and effort while keeping quality.
Continuous improvement: all employees constantly suggest and make small improvements to the way work is done.
Materials arrive only when needed and goods are made to meet orders, so very little stock is held.
A small team of workers makes a whole product or part, taking responsibility for its quality.
A small group of workers who meet regularly to find causes of quality problems and suggest solutions.
Design, production, marketing and purchasing work on a new product at the same time instead of in sequence.
Needs reliable suppliers, leaves little spare capacity, costs money to introduce and may meet resistance from workers.
Steady demand, reliable local suppliers and trained, stable staff favour it; unpredictable demand and unreliable supply make JIT risky.
Overproduction, waiting, unnecessary movement, excess stock, over-processing, defects and under-used skills.
